title: On Fatting the pigs for the winter market
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：fat　|　正文 367 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fat 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the fisherman ① fatted the pigs for the winter market for the whole place, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② fats the pigs for the winter market without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ fat the pigs for the winter market at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ fatted the pigs for the winter market before — a line in the logbook for July 1979 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Fatting the pigs for the winter market for the whole place, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ fat the geese on kitchen scraps without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Fat the geese on kitchen scraps at once and never mention it again.

By 1992 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ fats the geese on kitchen scraps for the whole place every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ fatted the pigs for the winter market again when nobody else would.

⑩ To fat the pigs for the winter market, my mother said in 1997, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody fats the pigs for the winter market without a word of thanks again and somebody must fat the pigs for the winter market for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 养肥（一般过去式 fatted the pigs for the winter market：1985 年渔人头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 养肥（一般现在 fats the pigs for the winter market：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 养肥（不定式 to fat the pigs for the winter market：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 养肥（过去完成时 had fatted the pigs for the winter market：1979 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 养肥（动名词 fatting the pigs for the winter market 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 使肥（fat the geese on kitchen scraps：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去使肥用厨下剩食把鹅喂肥）
G. v. 使肥（fat the geese on kitchen scraps：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 养肥（后段两处：新来的船工照例 fats the geese on kitchen scraps，而母亲又一次 fatted the pigs for the winter market）

fat 意为“养肥”，自那以后渔人不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 fats。
fat 意为“养肥”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯养肥为过冬的集市把猪养肥”，此处为不定式 to fat the pigs for the winter market。
fat 意为“养肥”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1992 年之前就有人养肥过，故用过去完成时 had fatted。
fat 意为“养肥”，渔人说“养肥为过冬的集市把猪养肥这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 fatting the pigs for the winter market 作主语。
fat 意为“使肥”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去使肥用厨下剩食把鹅喂肥”，should ever 之后用原形 fat the geese on kitchen scraps。
fat 意为“使肥”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻使肥用厨下剩食把鹅喂肥（fat the geese on kitchen scraps at once），以后再也不要提起。
fat 意为“养肥”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例使肥用厨下剩食把鹅喂肥，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 fats。
fat 意为“养肥”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人养肥为过冬的集市把猪养肥，用一般过去式 fatted 叙述。
fat 意为“养肥”，结尾那句是母亲 1997 年的话：要养肥为过冬的集市把猪养肥，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fat 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the fisherman fatted the pigs for the winter market for the whole place, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman fats the pigs for the winter market without a word of thanks whenever the harbour asks.
Fatting the pigs for the winter market for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever fat the geese on kitchen scraps without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour fats the geese on kitchen scraps for the whole place every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother fatted the pigs for the winter market again, and the harbour remembered that half.
